title: the ~500 non-error harness tests run in-process and never exercise src/bin/eu.rs
description:
Found by clarion during the eu-oxtcq gate audit, 2026-07-27, on master a1af1f0b.
Mechanism M6 of that inventory: a test that calls an entry point users do not hit.

WHAT WAS MEASURED

tests/harness_test.rs:54-56 runs an ordinary harness fixture as

    fn run_test(opt: &EucalyptOptions) {
        let exit_code = tester::test(opt).unwrap();

which goes tester::test -> tester::run_plans (src/driver/tester.rs:156) ->
InProcessTester -> driver::eval. It never spawns a binary. 506 tests are
generated from tests/harness/**, of which the ~330 non-error ones take this
in-process route. By contrast the error tests go through
tester::error_test_with_binary(eu_binary(), ..) (harness_test.rs:113) and the
typecheck tests spawn `eu check --strict` plus the eval path
(harness_test.rs:150-215), so those two families DO exercise the real binary.

WHY IT MATTERS

src/bin/eu.rs is not a thin wrapper. Lines 183-213 contain logic that exists
nowhere else:

  * the blob-core type-check dispatch --- `loader.prelude_blob()` decoded
    into prelude_units and handed to
    driver::check::run_type_checker_from_blob_core, with an explicit fallback
    to run_type_checker for a blob without baked cores. This is the ONLY
    non-test caller of run_type_checker_from_blob_core;
  * emission of the resulting type warnings to stderr via codespan_reporting.

So the largest test family in the project cannot observe either. This is the
same class as eu-vbctt (which is about `eu check` never reaching the
blob-core path) but an order of magnitude wider, and it compounds M11 /
eu-5yn9v: the harness fixtures that DO run under a blob in CI run via
`eu test tests/harness`, which does not include tests/harness/errors/** at
all, because those are generated Rust tests.

CONSEQUENCE

A regression confined to the eval-path blob-core dispatch --- a warning that
goes missing, a diagnostic sited differently, a fallback that stops firing ---
is invisible to ~330 harness tests, and the fixtures that would show it are
in the family that never runs under a blob. eu-rb5n was exactly this shape:
`065_lookup_key_typo_warns.eu` lost its warning on the eval path only, and a
dedicated single-file test had to be written for it after the fact
(test_eval_path_warns_on_record_key_typo).

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED

Coordinator ruling 2026-07-27: this is a harness-architecture change, not a
diagnostic bug, so its release status is for the owner to decide rather than
the coordinator. Filed with the measurements so that ruling can be made.

Options, roughly in increasing cost:
  1. Leave in-process as the default and add a small, explicit subprocess
     sweep over a chosen subset --- cheap, but reintroduces the allowlist
     mechanism the audit is trying to eliminate (M3).
  2. Give run_test a subprocess mode behind an env var, run it as an extra CI
     job. Measured cost is the concern: the in-process suite is ~43s; a
     process per fixture will be substantially more.
  3. Make the in-process path go through the same dispatch bin/eu.rs uses, by
     hoisting lines 183-213 of src/bin/eu.rs into a shared driver function
     both callers use. This removes the divergence rather than testing around
     it, and is the option that makes the other two unnecessary.

Related: eu-vbctt (same class, `eu check`), eu-5yn9v (blob-mode coverage is
an allowlist), eu-oxtcq (the parent audit; this is mechanism M6).
close_reason: Fixed by #1294 and #1298 (merged as a623450 and f1d1536). Re-closed by coordinator 20: the earlier close was lost when the relay refused a stale delta.

title: Audit every CI gate and test-infrastructure assertion for whether it can actually fail
description:
Five distinct dead or hollow gates were found in a single week (2026-07-20..27), all by accident while fixing something else. The common factor is not carelessness in any one change: it is that this project has several mechanisms by which a gate can look green while asserting nothing, and we have no systematic check for them.

The five found so far:
1. eu-7x0r / eu-5yn9v — blob-mode CI coverage was an ALLOWLIST (eu test on the .eu harness plus two named tests). All 174 error .expect fixtures ran source-prelude only.
2. eu-5yn9v — prelude_blob_ok is a build.rs cfg, so a '#![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]' test file compiles to ZERO tests without a blob. Absent coverage is indistinguishable from passing coverage.
3. eu-3skeg — build.rs needed an explicit rerun-if-changed for src/eval/intrinsics.rs; emitting ANY such directive opts cargo out of whole-package tracking, so the gate would have been silently dead.
4. eu-ziq8o — error .expect sidecars assert message TEXT but never source location. 083_array_arith_mismatch named the wrong declaration in every shipped release with a green test throughout.
5. eu-vbctt — test_config_matrix_blob_vs_source_prelude_byte_equal never exercises the blob-core path: it runs eu check, which always loads prelude source. Proven by injecting a fault that left it green while an eval-path equivalent went red.

Plus two near-misses inside individual fixes, where a fix's own new test would have PASSED without the fix: the eu-pazes complexity gate (ran in blob mode, where the old definition is linear) and the eu-r4647 safeguard (planted its Smid on an App node that synthesise_app never reads, so the warning carried Smid(None)).

TASK: enumerate the ways a gate here can silently not gate, then audit against that list rather than fixing instances as they surface. Candidate mechanisms to check for:
- cfg-gated test files that can compile to zero tests
- path-filtered workflows (.github/workflows/tree-sitter.yaml only triggers on certain paths, so job counts differ legitimately between PRs — but a genuinely required check could be filtered out unnoticed)
- allowlisted test selections inside CI jobs rather than whole-suite runs
- assertions matching on the wrong output channel (a regex that matches the 'stack trace:' note rather than the primary label line)
- tests whose fixtures are too small for the defect class (Smid/SourceMap/allocation-group bugs need LARGE fixtures)
- tests calling an entry point that is not the one users hit
- build-script staleness (a change that only takes effect at build time, with no dependency declared)

ACCEPTANCE: a written inventory of gate mechanisms and their failure modes; a pass over the existing suite against it; a bead per instance found; and where cheap, a meta-check that fails loudly (e.g. a test file contributing zero tests should be an error, not silence).

Owner context: 0.14 is the diagnostics release and the gate is 'diagnostics improvement PROVEN'. A proof mechanism that cannot fail proves nothing.
notes:
== INVENTORY OF GATE FAILURE MECHANISMS (clarion, 2026-07-27) ==

Measured on master a1af1f0b in a worktree, both prelude modes and both
engines. Blob generated locally; `prelude_blob_ok` confirmed from the
build-script output (target/debug/build/eucalypt-*/output), never inferred
from the blob file existing.

BASELINE: exactly three pre-existing blob-mode failures, all eu-7x0r ---
diagnostics_invariants::secondary_labels_do_not_excerpt_library_internals,
diagnostics_invariants::debug_trace_restores_the_uncurated_trace, and
harness_test::test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace. Nothing else.

--- M1. A cfg-gated compilation unit contributes zero tests, reports green.
DETECT: `cargo test --test X -- --list | grep -c ': test'` per target per
config.
MEASURED blob-less: diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test = 0 tests, exit 0. Every
other target non-zero (harness_test 506, lsp_test 111, io_args_test 12,
property_test 11, bytecode_io_differential_test 7, diagnostics_invariants 3,
diagnostics_json_emission 3, fuzz_regression_test 3, git_import_test 2,
conform_test 1, diagnostics_metadata_span_test 1, tick_parity_test 1). Grows
to three gated files as #1074 (ef1 deprecation gate) and #1085
(diagnostics_snapshots' two #[cfg(prelude_blob_ok)] tests) land.
CATCHES: a dropped/renamed `cargo xtask prelude-compile` step making a whole
job vacuous rather than red.
META-CHECK: DONE in PR #1095 (tests/gate_liveness.rs) --- a registry of every
conditionally compiled test file plus a STATIC check that each blob-gated
file's named CI job exists and runs prelude-compile, plus
EU_REQUIRE_PRELUDE_BLOB=1. Also DONE in PR #1094
(scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh fails when a target reports "0 passed").

--- M2. Path-filtered workflow.
Only .github/workflows/tree-sitter.yaml. Filter omits src/syntax outside
rowan/ and any new corpus directory; a genuinely required check could vanish
from the rollup and look normal, because job counts legitimately differ
between PRs.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): drop the path filter --- the job is short and
the filter buys nothing against the risk.

--- M3. Allowlisted test selection inside a CI job; a filter matching nothing
exits 0.
PROVEN: `cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants no_such_test -- --exact`
-> "test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 3 filtered out", exit 0.
INSTANCES: diagnostics-blob-mode job (2 selections); wasm job
(`cargo test --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib wasm_tests`).
The comment "Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands" had
nothing enforcing it.
FIX: DONE in PR #1094 --- scripts/diagnostics-gate.sh runs whole targets with
--skip and then requires each skipped test to STILL FAIL, so a fix turns the
job red until its line is deleted. wasm job NOT addressed.

--- M4. Assertion on the wrong channel, or a substring a note also satisfies.
172 of 174 error .expect sidecars assert message text only; 2 pin a
file:line:col. A pattern like "nth" is satisfied by the `stack trace:` note
even when the primary label is wrong --- 083_array_arith_mismatch shipped a
wrong location for releases with a green test (eu-ziq8o).
NEW INSTANCE FOUND: five error fixtures have NO sidecar
(008_op_spacing.eu, x007_bad_block_element.eu, x018_missing_comma.eu,
x021_dot_in_key.eu, x022_redef.eu). Only 008 has a generated test
(test_error_008 at harness_test.rs:1086); per `tester::error_test`'s own
doc, "If no .expect sidecar exists, the test is treated as unvalidated and
passes without running". That test does not execute its fixture at all and
cannot fail.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): give all five a sidecar, and make the tester
REJECT a sidecar-less error fixture rather than passing it --- the
silent-pass behaviour is the defect, the five instances are symptoms.

--- M5. Fixture too small for the defect class.
The invariant gate corpus --- the flagship "diagnostics PROVEN" gate --- is 9
fixtures, 21 lines TOTAL, max 4 lines, with region_start_line..region_end_line
spans of 1-2 lines inside 2-4 line files. Invariant (iii) is near-vacuous at
that size. Both headline defects of 0.14 are invisible in it BY
CONSTRUCTION: eu-og3u6 (anchor on the wrong declaration) needs >= 2 user
declarations; eu-7x0r / eu-r4647 (Smid aliasing) need a user SourceMap that
grows past the blob's ~7357 baked Smids. #1085 adds large fixtures but only
to the SNAPSHOT corpus, not this one.
PROPOSED (approved, NOT DONE): add fixtures large enough to catch both
classes, and reject a region spanning the whole file.

--- M6. Test calls an entry point users do not hit.
eu-vbctt confirmed (see that bead). LARGER INSTANCE, filed separately: the
~500 non-error harness tests run IN-PROCESS --- harness_test.rs:55
`tester::test(opt)` -> `tester::run_plans` -> `InProcessTester` ->
`driver::eval` --- bypassing src/bin/eu.rs, which is where the blob-core
type-check dispatch (`run_type_checker_from_blob_core`) and the type-warning
emission live. Only the error tests (`error_test_with_binary`) and the
typecheck tests spawn the binary.

--- M7. Build-script staleness / undeclared inputs.
build.rs emits 6 explicit rerun-if-changed, which opts out of whole-package
change tracking (eu-3skeg). NEW INSTANCE: BYTECODE_WIRE_FORMAT_VERSION = 5 is
declared TWICE --- build.rs:38 and xtask/src/main.rs:57 --- kept in step by
"MUST match" comments and nothing else. Divergence gives a permanent hash
mismatch -> prelude_blob_stale -> the blob path silently falls back to source
AND every cfg(prelude_blob_ok) test compiles to zero.
STATUS: already addressed by PR #1082 (moves the constant, the hash recipe,
the input paths and the staleness verdict into src/eval/stg/wire_format.rs
which build.rs include!s and xtask imports, and adds the missing
rerun-if-changed for the intrinsic catalogue). NOT duplicated here.
Also worth recording in build.rs: restoring a blob with `mv`/`cp -p`
preserves mtime, so cargo does not rerun build.rs and the stale cfg persists.

--- M8. (NEW) A skip that returns success.
`skip_on_windows` in #1085's tests/diagnostics_snapshots.rs (eu-1tkk.7.22) ---
an early `return` from the test body, i.e. green. Also
`tester::run_plans` (src/driver/tester.rs:173) silently skips a `requires-io`
plan when --allow-io is absent and continues with exit 0. Dormant today
(harness_test's io_opts grants it) but a new IO test added with plain
`opts()` would skip forever.
PROPOSED: skips should be counted and asserted against an expected count, or
expressed as #[ignore] so the runner reports them.

--- M9. (NEW) A relaxation that makes an assertion arm unreachable.
`assert!(heapsyn || unexpected_pass.is_empty())` in
corpus_satisfies_invariants. Separately, NO corpus fixture is marked
xfail today, so unexpected_pass is always empty and the arm was vacuous on
BOTH engines. The (iv) invariant's own comment in violations() is the model
for how to avoid this.
FIX: DONE in PR #1094 --- per-engine xfail_engines markers, the blanket
relaxation deleted, and the verdict extracted as a pure function with a unit
test per arm so the ratchet branch is provably reachable whatever the corpus
contains.

--- M10. (NEW) A duplicated constant kept in step by a comment.
eu-0cc1's TRACE_BUDGET (FIXED in PR #1094 by importing the crate constant);
M7's BYTECODE_WIRE_FORMAT_VERSION (PR #1082).
DETECT: grep for "MUST match", "shared with", "cannot drift apart".

--- M11. (NEW) Whole-suite coverage asymmetry between configurations.
The ONLY full `cargo test` in CI is the "Test Suite" job, which is
deliberately blob-less. Every blob-mode job runs `eu test tests/harness`,
which does NOT include tests/harness/errors/** --- those are generated Rust
tests in harness_test.rs. So all 174 error fixtures, the corpus that is
supposed to gate 0.14 diagnostics, run source-prelude ONLY. Proven:
test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace fails under a blob and no CI job can see
it. This is eu-5yn9v ("invert the default"), P1.

== STATUS ==
DONE (PRs open, not merged):
  #1094 fix/clarion-diagnostics-gate-infrastructure --- M3, M9, M10
        (TRACE_BUDGET), plus M1's per-target zero-test check; eu-1tkk.7.17,
        eu-0cc1.
  #1095 fix/clarion-gate-liveness --- M1 registry + static supplier check.
APPROVED BUT NOT STARTED: M2 (drop tree-sitter path filter), M4 (sidecars +
reject sidecar-less error fixtures), M5 (large invariant-corpus fixtures +
region validation).
FILED SEPARATELY: M6.
NOT MINE: M11/eu-5yn9v; M7 (PR #1082).

Every gate touched in #1094 and #1095 was fault-injection verified per site,
rebuilt each time --- 12 injections in total, listed in the two PR bodies.

title: error harness .expect sidecars assert message text but never source location
description:
Found while fixing eu-og3u6 (clarion, 2026-07-27).

Every error harness fixture under tests/harness/errors/ is gated by a
single stderr regex in its .expect sidecar. Almost all of them assert
only the message text (often just the fixture filename). None of the
nine fixtures whose diagnostics eu-og3u6 changed asserted the primary
label's file:line:col.

Consequence: a wrong-location regression is invisible to the harness.
083_array_arith_mismatch has been naming the wrong declaration in its
stack-trace note ('a', line 2, instead of 'c', line 4 — the declaration
that actually called arr.add) in every release that shipped it, with a
green test the whole time. eu-og3u6 itself survived because 193, the
one fixture that does assert a location, is a two-declaration file in
which the bug is invisible by construction.

0.14 is the diagnostics release; the corpus that is supposed to gate
diagnostics quality currently gates only message wording.

Proposal:
- require every error .expect regex to pin the primary label's own
  file:line:col, ahead of the 'stack trace:' marker so that a note-only
  match cannot satisfy it (194_og3u6_trace_anchor.eu.expect is the
  pattern to copy);
- audit the existing ~179 sidecars and add the assertion where the
  location is a meaningful property of the fixture;
- consider having the tester reject an error .expect whose regex
  contains no location, so the gap cannot reappear silently.

Related: eu-ntwg.2 (tester improvements).
notes:
DESIGN CONSTRAINT discovered the hard way (clarion, PR #1090, 2026-07-27). You CANNOT pin blob-only locations in .expect sidecars.

A .expect sidecar has NO NOTION OF PRELUDE MODE. The deliberately blob-less 'Test Suite' CI job runs the same fixtures, so a sidecar asserting a location that only exists under a blob fails that job. An agent tried exactly this and CI caught it - three fixtures red.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: 'require every error .expect regex to pin the primary label's file:line:col' cannot be applied uniformly. Locations that differ between blob and source mode, or exist in only one, must be asserted somewhere prelude-mode-aware. The working pattern is tests/diagnostics_blame_plumbing_test.rs - '#[cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]', run by the blob-mode job, reading the primary-label line via primary_label_position. Note the cfg-gated-file hazard: without a blob such a file compiles to ZERO tests and reports green, so the inventory must also fail loudly when a gated file contributes nothing.

So this bead needs a THREE-WAY split, not one rule: (a) locations identical in both modes -> pin in the .expect sidecar; (b) locations that differ or are blob-only -> assert in a prelude-mode-aware Rust test; (c) the 13-down-to-4 divergence inventory in tests/diagnostics/DIVERGENCE.md is the list of (b) cases.

ANCHOR PATTERN, verified: '┌─[^\n]*<fixture>\.eu:LINE:COL'. The [^\n]* cannot cross a line, and stripping the ┌─ line - leaving the location only in the 'stack trace:' note - was directly verified to give no match. Adopt this corpus-wide; matching the note instead of the label is a mistake made twice this week.

RELATED GATE WEAKNESS, same class as this bead: an .expect that pins a location can still be satisfied by to_diagnostic's TRACE FALLBACK rather than by the annotation plumbing under test. Demonstrated on 171_yaml_large_uint - replacing machine.annotation() with Smid::default() left the output byte-identical. So pinning a location gates that a correct label is PRESENT, not that the mechanism producing it works. Where the plumbing itself matters, it needs its own test.
close_reason: Fixed by #1294 and #1298 (merged as a623450 and f1d1536). Re-closed by coordinator 20: the earlier close was lost when the relay refused a stale delta.

comments.author: greg
comments.text:
From eu-1tkk.7.20 (furnace, PR #1089) — a fault-injection result eu-ziq8o should build in.

TIGHTENING A SIDECAR TO ASSERT THE LOCATION IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN.
The location assertion can pass for the wrong reason.

171_yaml_large_uint.eu.expect now asserts the primary label's file:line:col
anchored on the label line:

    ┌─[^\n]*171_yaml_large_uint\.eu:4:7

Verified the anchoring works: stripping the '┌─' line from the real stderr,
leaving the same location present only in the 'stack trace:' note, gives NO
match. So a note-only match cannot satisfy it — the property eu-ziq8o wants.

BUT it still does not gate the plumbing that produces the location. Fault
injection replacing machine.annotation() with Smid::default() at the error
construction site left the output BYTE-IDENTICAL and the test PASSED,
because ExecutionError::to_diagnostic falls back to searching env_trace then
stack_trace and recovered the same location from there.

So the assertion gates 'a correct primary label is present', not 'the error
carries the right Smid'. Where those two agree, a Smid regression is
invisible even to a location-asserting sidecar.

IMPLICATION FOR THE AUDIT: when adding a location assertion to a sidecar,
verify it can fail for the reason intended — break the Smid at the
construction site, not just the message — and record whether it gated. Where
the trace fallback masks it, either say so on the fixture or pick a fixture
whose error Smid and trace Smid differ.

The '┌─[^\n]*file\.eu:L:C' anchor plus the strip-the-label-line check is
offered as the corpus-wide pattern; the caveat above is the part a
mechanical sweep would otherwise miss.

Cross-ref: 194_toml_large_uint.eu.expect in the same PR uses the same shape.

Backfilled 291 locations identical in both prelude modes, 37 reasoned opt-outs. Known limit: in-process validate_error_test (eu test path) does not check locations (no rendered labels there). Close on merge.

title: [P1][ci] blob mode is the SHIPPED path but CI validates it by allowlist - invert the default
description:
REMAINING SCOPE (re-scoped 2026-08-03, post-0.14 housekeeping eu-bg55t): invert the PRIMARY cargo test configuration. The 'Test Suite' job in .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml (now explicitly named 'Test Suite (source-prelude fallback, no blob)') still runs the full cargo test suite blob-less, so blob mode — the shipped path — is validated by the dedicated 'Blob-mode cargo tests (all mode-sensitive targets)' job but is still not the PRIMARY cargo test configuration. Wanted: make blob mode the default configuration for the primary cargo test job, while KEEPING a deliberate, broad source-prelude job — furnace's 2026-07-27 measurement (comments below) shows a prelude-inlining defect class (e.g. eu-gua64, 2^N vs linear) is structurally observable ONLY in source mode, so the source job must run the harness suite, not a token invocation, and must fail loudly if it silently narrows.

HISTORY (original scope, filed 2026-07-26 under the owner directive 'this must end now, blob mode is the primary use case'): blob-mode CI coverage was an ALLOWLIST — the whole cargo test suite (all 174 error .expect fixtures, typecheck fixtures, unit tests) ran source-prelude only; cfg(prelude_blob_ok) files silently compiled to zero tests; the diagnostics-blob-mode job was scoped by --exact to exclude the known-red tests; and a stale workflow comment asserted phantom red typecheck tests. Four hiding mechanisms documented in the comments. DELIVERED since: eu-7x0r fixed (PR #1079, whole suite green under blob on both engines); scripts/blob-mode-tests.sh derives the mode-sensitive target list FROM THE TREE (17 targets, up from 4) with an EMPTY ratchet exclusion list; tests/gate_liveness.rs fails if discovery and registry drift, and requires the supplier job to RUN each target; EU_REQUIRE_PRELUDE_BLOB=1 makes a silently-ineffective blob a red job; job names state their mode (PR #1108, eu-1tkk.7.43, shipped in 0.14.0). Items (2) and (3) of the original WANTED list are done; item (1) — the primary-job inversion — is this bead's remaining scope.
notes:
FOURTH HIDING MECHANISM + A STALE BLOCKER, both verified by the coordinator against .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml lines 172-190 (2026-07-27).

MECHANISM 4 - the trap for an auditor. The 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' job DOES generate a blob and DOES invoke diagnostics_invariants - but scopes it to 'cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants corpus_satisfies_invariants -- --exact', excluding the two eu-7x0r tests by omission. The job comment names both tests and says 'Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands' - and NOTHING ENFORCES THAT WIDENING. So the one job that looks purpose-built to catch this class is deliberately scoped not to. An auditor sees a green job called 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' and concludes the area is covered. Widening it must be an explicit, tracked step of the inversion, not left to a comment.

Mechanisms 1 and 2 COMPOSE rather than overlap, confirmed concretely: test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace is tests/harness/errors/193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace.eu with a .eu.expect sidecar, driven only through run_error_test -> tester::error_test_with_binary under 'cargo test' - and 'cargo test' never runs under a blob.

STALE BLOCKER - GOOD NEWS, THE INVERSION IS LESS BLOCKED THAN THE COMMENT SAYS. The same comment claims 'harness-level typecheck tests 010/011/013/063/085 are actively red under blob mode (eu-rqwh, in progress)'. eu-rqwh was CLOSED on 2026-07-24, fixed and merged in PR #1059 (master f242bbc5). Wicket's verification on that PR explicitly confirmed all five typecheck tests pass BOTH with and without a blob, and recorded an 8 -> 3 master failure delta with the remaining three tracked as eu-7x0r. A blob-mode 'cargo test --no-fail-fast' on a1af1f0b independently shows test_193 as the only HARNESS failure.

CONSEQUENCE: the comment lists two blockers; only one is real. Once #1079 lands there is nothing left blocking the widening. Update or delete that comment as part of this bead - a stale CI comment asserting phantom red tests is itself a reason someone will decline to widen.
CLARION 2026-07-27, from the eu-oxtcq audit (mechanism M11). Two things
confirmed on master a1af1f0b that bear on this bead:

1. THE 010/011/013/063/085 CLAIM IS STALE. The comment in
   .github/workflows/build-rust.yaml asserting those harness-level typecheck
   fixtures are 'actively red under blob mode (eu-rqwh, in progress)' is
   false. eu-rqwh closed on 2026-07-24. Full `cargo test --test harness_test`
   with a verified blob (cargo:rustc-cfg=prelude_blob_ok read from the
   build-script output, not inferred from the file existing): all five pass.
   The ONLY failure in 506 tests was test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace, itself
   eu-7x0r. PR #1094 deletes the stale claim.

comments.text:
THE BLIND SPOT RUNS BOTH WAYS — keep a source-prelude job when inverting
(furnace, 2026-07-27, measured on master a1af1f0b while settling eu-pazes).

This bead documents blob-mode coverage that is absent. There is a symmetric
gap in the other direction, and inverting the default without care will
create it: BLOB MODE CANNOT GATE A PRELUDE-INLINING DEFECT AT ALL.

WHY. In blob mode the prelude arrives as already-compiled baked globals, so
the core inliner never sees prelude bodies and never beta-reduces them. On
the source path the prelude is compiled with the user's unit and IS inlined.
Any defect whose mechanism is "inlining a prelude combinator" is therefore
invisible to every blob-mode job, by construction — not flaky, not
under-covered, structurally unobservable.

MEASURED, same release binary, master a1af1f0b, superseded max-of,
`range(1, N) max-of`, timeout+heap-limit wrapped:

  config              N=16   N=20   N=22    N=1000  N=5000  N=20000
  source, ascending   124ms  699ms  2568ms  >90s    >90s    >90s
  blob,   ascending    44ms   41ms    43ms    47ms    72ms    153ms

Same binary, same expression, same input. Source mode is 2^N; blob mode is
linear and looks perfectly healthy at every size. The defect is real
(eu-gua64: `beta_reduce`, src/core/inline/reduce.rs:242, substitutes
arguments with no occurrence count, so a callee using a parameter twice —
`max(l, r): if(l > r, l, r)` — copies its caller's recursive call and gives
T(n) = 2·T(n-1)).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S ITEM (1). The single retained source-prelude job
is not a legacy courtesy or a fallback smoke test — it is the ONLY place this
class of defect can be caught. Please keep it, and keep it broad enough to
run the harness suite rather than a token invocation. "Invert the default"
must not become "delete source-mode coverage".

CONSEQUENCE FOR ITEM (2). The same reasoning applies to the loud-failure
requirement: a source-prelude job that silently narrows to a handful of tests
is the same failure mode as `#![cfg(prelude_blob_ok)]` compiling to zero
tests — absent coverage indistinguishable from passing coverage, just with
the polarity flipped.

WORKED EXAMPLE ALREADY IN TREE. `test_195_pazes_max_of_linear`
(tests/harness_test.rs, PR #1075) passes `--source-prelude` deliberately and
documents why: without the flag the test cannot fail even with the defective
definition restored, because blob mode measures it linear. That test is the
concrete shape of the coverage this bead must preserve.

Relevant to eu-1tkk.7.4 as well: golden diagnostics snapshots taken only in
the mode that ships will not capture regressions in prelude-inlined core
shape.

comments.text:
MECHANISM DETAIL from the eu-frf2o (PR #1087) CI review — three distinct mechanisms hide the blob-mode failures, not one. Whoever inverts the CI default needs all of them named, because fixing only the first leaves two intact.

Concrete specimens throughout: the three failures that are red on master under a blob and green in CI — secondary_labels_do_not_excerpt_library_internals, debug_trace_restores_the_uncurated_trace (both eu-7x0r) and test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace. All three fixed by PR #1079.

1. 'Test Suite' IS BLOB-LESS. Its only test steps are a bare 'cargo test' and 'cargo test --lib' (under EU_GC_STRESS); there is no prelude-compile step anywhere in the job. The workflow states the intent outright: 'the plain "Test Suite" job (deliberately blob-less, to keep the source-prelude fallback exercised)'. So its greenness is evidence about the SOURCE-PRELUDE configuration only. This is the mechanism already captured in the bead description.

2. THE BLOB HARNESS JOBS DO NOT VALIDATE errors/*.expect SIDECARS. 'Bytecode + blob harness' runs './target/release/eu test --allow-io tests/harness', i.e. the in-language .eu assertions only. The 174 error tests under tests/harness/errors/ are validated by their .expect sidecars (exit code + stderr regex) through harness_test.rs's run_error_test -> tester::error_test_with_binary, which only 'cargo test' drives — and 'cargo test' never runs under a blob (mechanism 1). Specimen: test_193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace is tests/harness/errors/193_1tkk_7_12_curated_trace.eu plus a .eu.expect sidecar. Nothing in CI checks that sidecar under a blob.

3. THE BLOB HARNESS JOBS NEVER RUN diagnostics_invariants AT ALL. It is a Rust integration test target (tests/diagnostics_invariants.rs), not a harness .eu file, so 'eu test tests/harness' cannot reach it by construction. That is where both eu-7x0r failures live.

4. (Fourth, and the trap for anyone auditing this quickly.) 'Diagnostics blob-mode integration' DOES generate a blob and DOES invoke diagnostics_invariants — but scopes it to 'cargo test --test diagnostics_invariants corpus_satisfies_invariants -- --exact', excluding the two eu-7x0r tests by omission. The workflow comment names both tests and eu-7x0r explicitly as the reason ('only tests confirmed to PASS under a blob today'). So the one job that looks like it should catch them is deliberately scoped not to. That scoping is correct as a stopgap, but it means widening this job is a required step of the eu-5yn9v inversion, not an optional one — the comment already says 'Widen the cargo test invocations below as each lands', and nothing enforces that.

Same comment also flags harness-level typecheck tests 010/011/013/063/085 as red under blob (eu-rqwh). I did NOT observe those locally on a1af1f0b — my blob run was 506 pass / 1 fail with test_193 the only harness failure — so that note may now be stale. Worth re-checking before it is used as a baseline.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING: I initially inferred from PR #1087's green board that the three failures were a macOS-local artefact. That was wrong, and it is exactly the reasoning this bead exists to kill. My own evidence already disproved it — the same machine ran 507/507 with EU_SOURCE_PRELUDE=1 and red under a blob, so the variable is the blob, not the platform. The inference is easy to make precisely because the board is comprehensive-looking (19 checks, several of them named '... blob harness'). Any fix for this bead should aim at making that inference correct rather than merely discouraged.

title: Compile strict arguments call-by-value (evaluate in place) instead of thunk-then-seq
description: From eu-oaz72.27 (PR #1158, docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-12-strict-accumulators.md). When demand analysis proves an argument strict, the compiler still allocates a thunk and then forces it (let x = thunk in seq x in f(x)). That costs about +3 ticks per iteration on strict accumulator loops (loop A at n=1e6: 37.0M to 40.0M ticks after #1158) and is the main obstacle to a foldl-strict that is cheaper than foldl. Compile a proven-strict argument by evaluating it in place, with no thunk. This is a compiler change only, with no new API; semantics are unchanged because strictness is proven. Starts after #1158 merges. eucalypt-backend and eucalypt-performance skills; any tick claim follows the measurement protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Loop A (from the report) at n=1e6 uses no more ticks than before #1158 while keeping constant stack; tick gate in a harness topic file, fault-injection verified; errors corpus unchanged in both prelude modes.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Design (2026-11-13): In ProtoAppGroup, a proven-strict (Strict, non-recursive) argument whose expression is a saturated strict arithmetic primop (the FUSIBLE_PRIMOP_NAMES set: ADD SUB MUL DIV GT GTE LT LTE) is compiled in place: case <arg> of _ -> ... with the value bound in a 1-slot case frame, instead of let thunk + seq. Restricted to that set because a case continuation strips metadata whereas thunk+Update memoises a Meta value; these primops never return a Meta, so the value passed is identical. LetBinder's strict_indices become ordered strict steps (Force(binding) or Evaluate(proto)) realised in argument order, so evaluation order of strict args is unchanged; lazy binding refs are bumped past the case frames. Other strict args keep thunk+seq. Gate: tick budget for loop A in a harness topic file, fault-injected in both dispatch modes; laziness and errors corpus checked in blob and source prelude modes. Baseline on master c6e2036: loop A n=1e6 = 40,000,191 ticks, max stack 7 (measured-single).

Causes: (1) the case scrutinee runs inside the call's let frame (stamped with the call smid) where the thunk closed over the enclosing frame; (2) a Branch continuation does not restore the live annotation as SeqBind does, and its fallback frame is stamped with the scrutinee's leftover annotation. errors/ corpus does not exercise it. A compiler-only fix cannot reproduce master's stamps in general. comments.text: Design (2026-11-17, resumed): compiler-only first, engine only if diagnostics demand it. Since #1179, master's Branch continuation restores the annotation live at push (eu-oaz72.63), which removes #1179's second cause. The first cause (scrutinee inside the call's let frame) is removed by evaluating in-place args BEFORE the let: Ann(call) [Case(arg0, _ -> Case(arg1, _ -> Let(lazy and other strict args, Seq..., call))))]. Each scrutinee runs in the enclosing env (where the thunk would have closed), under the call's annotation (as SeqBind/Update did). Eligible: a strict, non-recursive, updatable (not skip_update) arg that is a saturated fusible primop (ADD SUB MUL DIV GT GTE LT LTE: no Meta results), and only the eligible args forming a PREFIX of the strict args in argument order, so strict evaluation order is exactly master's. Case-bound slots are referenced from inside the let by offset past the let frame; lazy bindings resolve through synthetic size-1 contexts. Checks: reviewers' #1179 error cases byte-identical to master (both prelude modes, both dispatch modes), new error fixtures, tick gate, errors corpus both modes. No change to bytecode/*, wire_format.rs, analyse*, prelude.

Resumed 2026-11-17: STOPPED for an owner decision. Branch eu-oaz72.67/strict-args-call-by-value (WIP commit 3278024, no PR).

Tried compiler-only: Ann(call, Case(arg0, _ -> Case(arg1, _ -> Let(rest, Seq.., call)))) with in-place args = strict, non-recursive, updatable fusible-primop args forming a prefix of the strict args (evaluation order = master). The #1179 reviewer cases where the error is in the FIRST in-place arg now match master (Branch restores the annotation since eu-oaz72.63). But any error in a LATER argument of the same call (a second in-place arg, or a lazy/strict thunk arg) gains a 'called from here' label at the call: each case frame is stamped with the Branch's pushed annotation (the call's), and later args run in an env containing it. Stack traces are identical; only the env trace gains the call smid. Variant with the cases outside Ann(call) is worse (stack trace loses the call). Ann(default) cannot clear the annotation (no-op under predecode). So a compiler-only fix cannot match master.

Touches bytecode/{machine,cont,encode,predecode,opcode}.rs, stg/{syntax,arena,optimiser,embed,pretty,materialise}.rs and the wire format (v12). Two reviews. Collides with open #1268 (eu-oaz72.175), which changes the same machine.rs/encoder paths, introduces closed bindings over an annotation spine (which changes what a thunk's env trace contains) and takes wire v11. Recommend: do it after #1268 merges, designed against its spine.

title: Strict accumulation: foldl-strict and demand analysis for self-recursive accumulators
description: A counter loop to 1e6 grows the stack two frames per iteration because the accumulator stays lazy; forcing it in the condition gives O(1) stack. 1e6-step simulations take 3-20 s and 2-11 GB; 1e7 is out of reach. A `seq`/strict-fold primitive (or demand analysis proving strictness for self-recursive accumulators) would make tight loops viable.
design:
Design (2026-11-12, implementing agent):
1. Demand analysis (src/core/analyse_demand.rs):
 a. Signature frames: a stack parallel to de Bruijn scopes (one frame per Let/Lam). A saturated call through Var::Bound to a let-bound lambda uses that binding's signature (pessimistic lazy_multi when unknown or partially applied).
 b. analyse_let analyses RHSs before the body. Lambda bindings start from an optimistic signature (strict_once per parameter) and the RHSs are re-analysed until every lambda binding's signature is stable (joint fixpoint over the let group; only iterates when a RHS consulted the group's own signatures). Stale pointer-keyed signatures from discarded iterations are rolled back. Iteration cap: on reaching it, signatures are set pessimistic and the group analysed once more (a post-fixpoint, so sound).
 c. IF: a variable strict in both branches is strict (branch lub on strictness only; cardinality unchanged, conservative).
 d. Lambda value (not directly applied): captured variables are Lazy, not the body's strictness unscaled. Fixes the #1156 open note, observable on master: k(a): {y: •}.(a + y); k(panic("x")) block? panics.
 Loop A, loop(a, n): if(n = 0, a, loop(a + 1, n - 1)), then has a strict -> the recursive call Seqs a + 1.
2. Prelude: foldl-strict(op, i, l), same signature as foldl, forcing the accumulator to WHNF each step (owner decision on this bead + plan s6). foldl unchanged. sum, product, count use foldl-strict (observably identical: + and * are strict, count never forces elements).
Untouched: lambda literal in function position signature lookup keyed on the pre-analysis body pointer (#1156 note 2).
acceptance_criteria: foldl-strict documented and typed, range(0, 1e6) foldl-strict(+, 0) in constant stack and fewer ticks than foldl; foldl behaviour unchanged (test with a lazy accumulator that relies on it); demand analysis makes loop A's accumulator strict (stack and ticks measured before/after under the protocol); tests fault-injection verified.
notes: 2026-11-12 owner decisions: foldl must NOT change (keep its lazy accumulator semantics). Provide a separate strict variant named foldl-strict (foldl' is not possible: a single quote starts a quoted identifier). Second part: demand analysis should prove self-recursive accumulators strict (loop A in the if/then bug: 2 extra frames/iter from the a + 1 + 1 ... chain) - a compiler improvement, not a language feature. A seq primitive only if that proves insufficient. Related: the if/then tail-position bug (constant stack is a prerequisite for measuring this).

comments.text:
eu-sd41o sweep (PR #1302): item (1) was built and then reverted, because the coordinator ruled that it changes documented semantics, which is the owner's call. Item (2), Int/UInt/Float GC test elements in machine.rs, landed in #1302.

Options for item (1), the representative kept when 1 and 1.0 meet as one set element or dict key:

A. Always prefer the integer, whatever the order of insertion, union or merge. It is canonical, and equal sets render identically. This was built and tested in #1302 commit 1777e9f (Dict::canonical_key) before the revert.
   Doc-string changes in lib/prelude.eu:
   - dict.of: "the first key and the last value are kept" -> "the integer form of the key (1 over 1.0) and the last value are kept".
   - dict.assoc: "that key is kept and only its value replaced" -> "the key's integer form is kept and the value replaced".
   - dict.merge-with: "a's key is kept" -> "the integer form of the key is kept".
   - set docs (set.of, set.add, set.union): add "of equal numbers, the integer form is kept".
   - Also: the src/eval/stg/dict.rs DictMergeWith comment, and docs/guide/dicts.md and sets.

B. Keep the first inserted (as documented for dicts today), and make sets and set union match: left operand wins in union and intersection, first wins in from-list and add. No dict doc changes are needed. Set docs gain "of equal numbers (1 and 1.0), the first inserted is kept; in union the left operand's". Equal sets can still render differently (1 vs 1.0) depending on construction order.

C. Render-only canonicalisation: keep storage as now, but render a whole-number float key as an integer. This changes output for genuine float keys, which is a bigger change. Not recommended.

Recommendation: A. It is the only option that makes "equal sets render the same", which is the defect the bead reports. It is already implemented and fault-injection tested, and in AoC-style use integer keys are the common case.
